title: Migration of the Prophet [pbuh]
arabicTitle: هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

topics.title: Migration of the Prophet [pbuh]

paragraphs.text: When the iniquitous decision had been made, Gabriel was sent down to Muhammad (Peace be upon him) to reveal to him Quraish's plot and give him his Lord's Permission to leave Makkah. He fixed for him the time of migration and asked him not to sleep that night in his usual bed. At noon, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) went to see his Companion Abu Bakr and arranged everything for the intended migration. Abu Bakr was surprised to see the Prophet (Peace be upon him) masked, coming to visit him at that unusual time, but he soon learned that Allah's Command had arrived, and he proposed that they should migrate together, to which the Prophet (Peace be upon him) gave his consent.

To implement their devilish plan, the chiefs of Makkah had chosen eleven men: Abu Jahl, Hakam bin Abil Al-'As, 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ait, An-Nadr bin Harith, Omaiyah bin Khalaf, Zama'a bin Al-Aswad, Tu'aima bin 'Adi, Abu Lahab, Ubai bin Khalaf, Nabih bin Al-Hajjaj and his brother Munbih bin Al-Hajjaj. As night advanced, they posted assassins around the Prophet's house, keeping vigil all night, waiting to kill him the moment he left early in the morning. Abu Jahl jeered at Muhammad's words, saying to those around him: "Muhammad claims that if you follow him, he will appoint you rulers over the Arabs and non-Arabs, and in the Hereafter your reward will be Gardens; otherwise he will slaughter you and after death you will be burnt in fire."

Allah, the All-Mighty, however, did exactly what He later said: "And (remember) when the disbelievers plotted against you [O Muhammad (Peace be upon him)] to imprison you, or to kill you, or to get you out (from your home); they were plotting and Allah too was planning, and Allah is the Best of the planners." [8:30] Despite the tight siege, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) told 'Ali to sleep in his bed and cover himself with his green mantle, assuring him no harm would come to him. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) then came out, cast a handful of dust at the assassins, and worked his way through them reciting: "And We have put a barrier before them, and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them up, so that they cannot see." [36:9] He proceeded to the house of Abu Bakr, and both set out southwards, clambered up the lofty peak of Mount Thawr, and took refuge in a cave.

The assassins were waiting for the zero hour when someone informed them that the Prophet (Peace be upon him) had already left. They rushed in and, to their utter surprise, found 'Ali lying in the Prophet's bed, not Muhammad (Peace be upon him). This created a stir in the whole town. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) had thus left his house on Safar 27th, the fourteenth year of Prophethood, i.e. 12/13 September 622 A.D. Knowing that Quraish would mobilize all its potential to find him, he played a clever trick: instead of taking the road to Madinah north of Makkah, he walked along a road least expected, lying south and leading to Yemen, until he reached the rough rocky Mount Thawr, five miles away.

Abu Bakr (May Allah be pleased with him) carried him up the mountain to a cave called after it, Cave Thawr. Abu Bakr first entered to explore the cave, closed all its holes with pieces torn from his clothes, cleaned it, and then asked the Prophet (Peace be upon him) to step in. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) went in and laid his head in Abu Bakr's lap and fell asleep. Suddenly Abu Bakr's foot was stung by a poisonous insect; it hurt so much that his tears fell on the Prophet's face. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) applied his saliva to the foot and the pain went off on the spot. They confined themselves to this cave for three nights — Friday, Saturday and Sunday. 'Abdullah, the son of Abu Bakr, would visit after dusk and apprise them of the situation in Makkah; and 'Amir bin Fuhairah used to bring goats every evening to furnish them with a plentiful supply of milk.

Quraish, baffled when the news of the escape was confirmed, brought 'Ali to Al-Ka'bah and beat him brutally, then went to see Asma', Abu Bakr's daughter; Abu Jahl slapped her so severely that her earring broke. The notables convened an emergency session, decided to block all avenues out of Makkah, imposed heavy armed surveillance, and set a price of 100 camels upon the head of each of the two men. Horsemen and trackers scoured the country, and once even reached the mouth of the cave. Seeing the enemy so close, Abu Bakr whispered: "What if they were to look through the crevice and detect us?" The Prophet (Peace be upon him), in God-inspired calm, replied: "Silence Abu Bakr! What do you think of those two with whom the Third is Allah?"

'Abdullah bin Uraiquit, who had not yet embraced Islam but was trusted and hired by Abu Bakr as a guide, reached the cave after three nights with the two camels. The opportunity to depart had come. Abu Bakr offered the Prophet (Peace be upon him) the swift animal to ride, and the latter agreed provided he would pay its price. They took the food provisions that Asma' had tied in a bundle from her waistband, which she tore into two — hence her appellation, 'Asma' of the two waistbands'. The Prophet (Peace be upon him), Abu Bakr and 'Amir bin Fuhairah departed, their guide leading them along the coastal route. That was in Rabi' Al-Awwal, 1st year A.H. (September 622 A.D.).

Quraish had declared that whoever seized Muhammad (Peace be upon him) would receive a hundred camels. Among those who set out to win the reward was Suraqah, son of Malik. He mounted a swift horse and pursued them, but the horse stumbled and threw him; drawing lots, he found the omens unpropitious, yet the lust for wealth blinded him and he resumed the chase. The horse stumbled repeatedly, and when he came close, Suraqah realized it was a warning from Allah. He approached penitently, begged forgiveness, and informed them of Quraish's reward. He offered them provisions, which they declined, asking only that he screen their departure. The Prophet (Peace be upon him) forgave him and confirmed it with a written token. The sworn enemy was thus converted into an honest believer who hurried back to foil the other pursuers. In Abu Bakr's version: "None caught up with us except Suraqah... I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, this one has caught up with us.' He replied: 'Don't be cast down, verily, Allah is with us.'"

The party continued until it reached the tents of a woman called Umm Ma'bad Al-Khuza'iyah, a gracious lady who sat at her tent-door for any passing traveller. Fatigued and thirsty, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) wanted food and milk; she said the flock was out at pasture and the goat standing nearby was almost dry, for it was a rainless year. With her permission, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) touched its udders, reciting the Name of Allah, and plenty of milk flowed. He offered it first to the lady, then shared it, then refilled the container for her and left. When her husband Abu Ma'bad returned and saw the milk, his wife described the blessed visitor; Abu Ma'bad realized it was the man Quraish were seeking, and later composed verses of poetry in his admiration that echoed across Makkah — and from which Asma' learned that the two companions were heading for Madinah.

On the way, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) met Abu Buraidah, one of those lured by Quraish's reward; no sooner did he talk with the Prophet (Peace be upon him) than he embraced Islam along with seventy of his men, and took off his turban and tied it to his lance as a banner. They also met Az-Zubair at the head of a caravan returning from Syria, who presented them two white garments. On Monday, 8th Rabi' Al-Awwal, the fourteenth year of Prophethood (23rd September 622), the Messenger of Allah arrived at Quba'.

As the news of Muhammad's arrival spread, crowds came flocking out of Madinah every morning, waiting eagerly until forced back by the midday heat. One day, after they had retired, a Jew, catching a glimpse of three travellers clad in white, shouted from a hillock: "O you people of Arabia! Your grandfather has come! He whom you have been waiting for has come!" The Muslims rushed out to greet their noble guest. Ibn Al-Qayyim said: "The shouts of 'Allahu Akbar' resounded in Banu 'Amr bin 'Auf," and the Revelation was sent down: "...then verily, Allah is his Maula (Protector), and Gabriel, and the righteous among the believers — and furthermore, the angels — are his helpers." [66:4] Banu 'Amr bin 'Awf hosted him on that Monday in Rabi' Al-Awwal, and when the sun grew hot, Abu Bakr stood up to shade him.

The Prophet (Peace be upon him) stayed in Quba' with Kulthum bin Al-Hadm, a hospitable chief of 'Amr bin 'Awf, for four days — Monday to Thursday — during which the foundation of Quba' Mosque was laid on the basis of pure piety. 'Ali hung back in Makkah for three days to return the trusts to their owners on behalf of the Prophet (Peace be upon him), then followed to join him at Quba'.

On Friday morning, the Prophet (Peace be upon him) sent for Bani An-Najjar, his maternal uncles, to escort him to Madinah. He halted in the vale of Banu Salim and performed his Friday prayer with a hundred others. The tribes and families of Madinah — the new name for Yathrib, short for 'The Messenger's Madinah (City)' — came streaming forth, vying with one another in inviting the noble visitor, and the girls chanted beautiful verses of welcome. Every Ansar was eager to host the Messenger. He answered everyone courteously: "This camel is commanded by Allah; wherever it stops, that will be my abode." The camel moved on with slackened rein, knelt at the site of the Prophetic Mosque, rose, returned and knelt again in the same spot. He alighted in the quarter of Banu Najjar, related to him on the maternal side; the fortunate host, Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, welcomed him into his house.

A few days later there arrived the Prophet's spouse Sawdah, his two daughters Fatimah and Umm Kulthum, Usama bin Zaid, Umm Aiman, and 'Abdullah son of Abu Bakr with Abu Bakr's household including 'Aishah (May Allah be pleased with her). Zainab was not able to emigrate and stayed with her husband Abi Al-'As till the Battle of Badr. 'Aishah said: "When the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him) arrived in Madinah, both Abu Bakr and Bilal fell ill," reciting verses of homesickness in their fever. She briefed the Prophet (Peace be upon him), and he prayed: "O Allah, make us love Madinah as much as we used to love Makkah, or even more. O Allah, bless and increase the wealth of Madinah, and transmute its rotten mud into wholesome edible fat."

topics.topicSummary: When Quraish plotted to assassinate him, Gabriel warned the Prophet ﷺ and permitted migration. 'Ali slept in his bed as a decoy while the Prophet ﷺ slipped past the assassins reciting [36:9] and joined Abu Bakr. They hid three nights in the Cave of Thawr — where Allah blinded the pursuers ('What do you think of two with whom the Third is Allah?'). Guided south then along the coast, they survived Suraqah's pursuit (who converted) and Umm Ma'bad's hospitality, reaching Quba' on 8th Rabi' Al-Awwal. After founding Quba' Mosque, the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah, where his camel chose the mosque's site and Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari hosted him.

The Prophet ﷺ slipped past the assassins, reciting [36:9], and joined Abu Bakr
